questions.question: Explain the difference between internal and external factors in a SWOT analysis, and classify: (a) the owner has a driver's licence; (b) a competitor opens nearby; (c) the business has little capital; (d) office parks with large parking areas nearby.
questions.expected_answer: Internal factors (strengths and weaknesses) belong to the business and it can control them; external factors (opportunities and threats) come from the environment and the business can only respond to them. (a) strength, internal; (b) threat, external; (c) weakness, internal; (d) opportunity, external.

questions.question: A survey of 50 car owners found that 32 would use a mobile car wash. Calculate the percentage, and explain how Shine on Wheels can use its water-saving method to deal with the threat of water restrictions.
questions.expected_answer: 32 ÷ 50 × 100 = 64 percent. The method uses about 20 litres per wash instead of about 150 litres with an open hose, so the business can keep operating during most restrictions and can market itself as water-wise: a strength used against a threat, which turns the threat into a selling point.

questions.question: Distinguish between a feature and a benefit, give one example of each for Shine on Wheels, and state its unique selling point.
questions.expected_answer: A feature is a fact about the product; a benefit is what the customer gains from it. Feature: we wash the car where it is parked. Benefit: the customer saves time, for example an hour of the weekend. USP: a convenient, water-wise car wash at the customer's home or workplace.
